title: The other half: topic and comment
summary: Every sentence has a が carriage and also a は topic, visible or not. The comment after the topic is always a full logical clause.

blocks.text: Japanese has two structures at once. The **logical** one (carriage and engine) is ruled by **が**. The **non-logical** one (topic and comment) is ruled by **は**. A sentence always has a が carriage, and in the same way it always has a **は topic**, even when you cannot see it.

A topic is what the conversation is currently about. English tracks it with pronouns: "I had a ball. I dropped it. It rolled away. Sakura picked it up." The ball is sometimes an object, sometimes a subject, so what is tracked is not the subject but the topic. Japanese just tracks it with は, or leaves it out as a zero.

Sentences like コーヒーが好きだ, 頭が痛い, お腹が空いた and クレープが食べたい are complete logical clauses where the carriage is not the person. To be grammatically complete they also need an invisible topic: "in relation to me, coffee is likable". Usually the topic is "I", but not always.
（私は）コーヒーが好きだ。 As for me, coffee is likable.
Seeing a tall person, you can say the sentence below with an invisible topic that points to that person, not to yourself.

blocks.en: (You) are tall, aren't you! (The unseen topic is the person you are looking at.)

blocks.text: The comment is a full clause

は can never mark the carriage or the engine, so a topic sentence has only **two** parts: the topic and the comment. Both elements of the logical clause must be **inside the comment**. So the comment is always a **complete logical clause**. This is not a random rule, but a consequence of the structure.
象は鼻が長い。 The comment 鼻が長い is a full clause: it has its own carriage and engine.

blocks.en: As for elephants, the nose is long.
In this town, summer is hot.
As for me, the head hurts.

blocks.text: は or が is really a choice of what to show

People ask "は or が?" as if both did the same job. They do not. Since the topic and the carriage are both always present, you are really deciding which to make visible. Each choice has a slightly different feeling.

rows: As for me, I am American (maybe others are not)
I am the one who is American

items: Two structures: **carriage + engine** (が) and **topic + comment** (は).
A topic can be invisible, just like a zero carriage.
The **comment** is always a full logical clause with its own carriage and engine.
は and が are not alternatives; they show different parts of the sentence.

questions.instruction: Which particle rules the topic-and-comment structure?
questions.note: が rules carriage and engine; は rules topic and comment.

questions.instruction: What is a topic?
options: The thing that does the verb
What the conversation is currently about
The thing the verb is done to
The last word of a sentence
questions.note: English tracks the topic with pronouns; Japanese uses は or a zero.

questions.instruction: What is the comment in a topic sentence?
options: A complete logical clause with its own carriage and engine
questions.note: は cannot mark the carriage or engine, so both must sit inside the comment.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.note: は sets the topic; 耳が長い is the comment.

questions.instruction: Tap the topic
questions.en: At this school, the teachers are kind.
questions.note: は marks the topic; 先生が親切だ is the comment.

questions.instruction: Tap the carriage of the comment
questions.en: My younger brother is fast on his feet.
questions.note: Inside the comment, 足 is the carriage of 速い.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.note: Topic, then a comment with carriage and engine.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: My older sister has long hair.
questions.en: My older sister has long hair.
questions.note: 姉は is the topic; かみが長い is the comment.

questions.instruction: What is the invisible topic here?
questions.note: With no context, the zero topic is usually I.

questions.instruction: You point at a tall stranger and say 背が高いね. Who is the invisible topic?
options: The person you are looking at
questions.note: The invisible topic is whatever the talk is about.

questions.instruction: Which sentence has a visible topic and a comment with its own visible carriage?
questions.note: 兄は is the topic; 料理が上手だ is a full clause.

questions.instruction: True or false? は can mark the carriage of a sentence.
questions.note: は can never mark the carriage or the engine: it marks the topic.

questions.instruction: Which noun is the carriage of 好きだ?
questions.note: 好きだ is built on an adjectival noun: the cat is the one being liked.

questions.instruction: Which version shows the topic but leaves the carriage invisible?
questions.note: You choose what to show: neither, the topic (は) or the carriage (が).

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.en: This car has a beautiful color.
questions.note: Inside the comment, 色 is the carriage of きれいだ.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.note: は sets the topic for a full comment 歌が上手だ.

questions.instruction: Tap the engine of the comment
questions.note: 好きだ is the engine; 犬 is its carriage.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: This room has a big window.
questions.en: This room has a big window.
questions.note: Topic (この部屋は), then the comment (窓が大きい).

questions.instruction: "I had a ball. I dropped it. It rolled away." What does English track with the pronouns?
questions.note: The ball changes role; what stays is the topic.

questions.instruction: How many parts does this sentence have?
options: Three: 犬は, 目が, 大きい
Two: the topic (犬は) and the comment (目が大きい)
questions.note: A topic sentence has just topic and comment.

questions.instruction: True or false? A sentence can have a topic even when you cannot see one.
questions.note: The topic, like the carriage, can be an invisible zero.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: Our house has a big yard.
questions.en: Our house has a big yard.
questions.note: Topic, then a comment with its own carriage and engine.
